key_insight: CDSE improves LLM agent skills by splitting each skill into four coordinated functions—Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script—rather than treating skills as one undifferentiated artifact.
engineering_relevance: For practical agent systems, this suggests skill stores and update pipelines should be designed around function-specific memory, validation, and invocation to improve transfer, planning, and tool use.
method: Extract evidence-grounded gradients from successful and failed trajectories
Consolidate updates by functional role into Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script components
Use cross-component coordination plus adaptive invocation to validate and apply updates
evidence_signal: The paper reports that 96.8% of 500 top-ranked skill packages span at least two functional roles, and CDSE achieves the best results in all 36 benchmark settings across six benchmarks, three agent models, and two harnesses.
watch_item: The approach adds system complexity, so robust component routing and validation are important to avoid brittle updates or misallocation of knowledge.
paper_title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
